newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil-U.S. group casts lone bid on power project.
newsitem.headline: Brazil-U.S. group casts lone bid on power project.

text.p: A consortium including U.S.-owned Alcoa Aluminio S.A. was the sole bidder for a contract to build a hydropower plant in the southern Brazilian state of Rio Grande do Sul, officials said.

A state spokeswoman told Reuters the group bid on a contract to build a 125-megawatt (MW) hydro plant, estimated by the state to cost $135 million, on the Jacui River about 217 miles (350 kms) from the state capital of Porto Alegre.

The consortium, also made up of local firms Camargo Correa Industrias, Inepar SA Industria e Construcoes (Inepar), Centrais Eletricas Santa Catarina SA and units of Brazilian groups Gerdau GER.RJ and Votorantim, submitted its proposal to the state's Bidding Commission at a 1000 local/0700 est.
Details of the technical and financial proposal were not revealed. A winner will not be named until Feb 4 and a contract signed on Feb 14, she said.
The spokeswoman for the state's Energy, Mines and Communications Office said the financial bids will be opened Jan 30.

Construction on the Dona Francisca plant, which will include two 62.5-MW turbines and tie into the state's power grid, will begin sometime between April and June and will take 47 months to complete, she added.
Alcoa has an 18.17 percent stake and Camargo Correa a 15.67 percent stake, the spokeswoman said.
Inepar, owned by Parana state, has a 25-percent stake and Santa Catarina state-owned Centrais Eletricas de Santa Catarina (Celesc) holds 15-percent of the consortium, she said.
Cia de Cimento Portland Gaucho of the Votorantim Group owns 13.15 percent and Gerdau unit Santa Felicidade Comercio, Importacoes e Exportacoes S.A. holds a 13 percent stake, she added.
